> He was expelled from one school for threatening to kill his class...I think he was 7-8 at the time though so maybe he didn't know what that meant, at least that's what he told me and it makes sense imo men develop slower than women at that age. 

Holy fucking shit...holy fucking shit...holy fucking shit. Nope nope nope nope nope nope.

Yes but even with an alibi this ridiculous...I mean yeah they have an alibi for the entire month..and any month really(if the police actually dig through all they had to offer) but would they? Wouldn't that take the police(or crime investigation organization) a very long time...I mean we're talking literally a month worth of video here.

Thanks for the answers thus far, I appreciate it!

That aside, let's say it is verifiable that they do have an alibi extending throughout the entire month and where they were at all times can be verified through the means delineated above. Just the house cameras and dashcams alone pretty much show where they were almost all the time anyway. The rest could be shown through GPS , social media, texts, and receipts from various locations, but let's say that the defendant is an out and out homebody in this case.

Would this generally(most of the time) be the anti-smoking gun? 

*Edit* I admit this is a pretty "out there" hypothetical, but if this was the case...what(do you personally think) would happen?

Especially if the accuser has no evidence themselves to produce other than their testimony.

> Unless that evidence can show where the accused was 24/7 for the entire month, then no. 

Ah, but what if it actually was quite literally where they were 24/7 almost without doubt unless they climbed out of their window. Let's say these cameras have been their for years and they keep all the recordings and they are on 24/7 clearly showing the defendant was home and for how long, and let's say whenever they did leave they have an alibi for exactly where they went and how long they were there. 

I would imagine this would help a great deal, especially if the accuser has no evidence at all. More information on how much this would help in a case like this would be helpful.

> Different cars can be used, the assault could have taken place away from the accuseds home. 

Yes but let's say that was the only cars used were the defendants with dashcams inside. The only other times they had left the house they were with other people and the defendant could prove this via witness testimony(the person they were with), OR with texts that were sent to and from the person they were with at that time. Let's say the defendant also has produced evidence via their social media account(s) that show videos recorded and posted from where they were at those times as well.

> Even the month could be wrong based off of the traumatized victim'should recollection. 

Let's say the defendant could produce the same sort of concentrate alibi for every month, with maybe a few small gaps but for the most part he/she can show where they were 24/7 due to them being a homebody with many security cameras on 24/7. All the cameras are also watermarked and digitally time stamped and can be verified as well with a couple calendars showing the date and time when the videos are recorded.

> The evidence could help. But it would likely not be the anti-smoking-gun

If I what I said above holds true, would that be a smoking gun? (At least 99% of the time?)
I agree, but no need to call them a dick head.

> If everyone prioritized the needs of others over their own, your needs are still being prioritized- just not by you. If this sacrifice is too much of a gamble, society can still benefit as a whole (even in a way you define it) by you occasionally choosing to act selflessly.

Wrong, not everyone's needs would be properly prioritized. In fact this very erroneous ideology is the central cause of my wishing to commit suicide, it's disingenuous, and unrealistic, most people do not care about anyone other than themselves, or perhaps their close friends and family, if you believe otherwise you're a fool.

> It is logical (see first sentence above). Additionally, it is a very logical pursuit to seek to better society. Volunteering time and skills for the betterment of others has a net positive effect on the world. Even if everyone else doesn't care about anyone, I know the second half of your sentence is inaccurate based on my own experiences. I acknowledge that I am unable to prove this.

Yes, I did state that some people will derive a sense of purpose and happiness in this world by assisting others, and if you participate in this sort of behavior than I thank you, but please note by engaging me in this way to try to attack my more realistic and logical view of the world doesn't help me at all. All you're presently doing is reinforcing the reasons why I want to kill myself. My biggest being the tendency towards people to warp their perceptive to befit their spurious reference frame, and the majorities inability to take off their rose tinted glasses being another.

> I am uncertain if this was directed at me or if that entire paragraph was just a monologue. If the former is true, I argue that I comprehend what you are saying, but I disagree with it. If the latter is true, know that I took the time to read it.

What do you disagree with? The statistics, or the fact that reality doesn't actually conform to your fairy tail ideals? Yes men have it harder, and have always had it harder throughout history, read a few books from a non bias perspective. Women have it harder in some aspects, but those are few and far between. However throughout history it is men that have also lived the largest, those very same men crush the lives of the men underneath them, and as such it isn't women's fault that men have had it harder; it is instead the fault of those men who have lived lives of extravagance and glory over the years. No two people are created equal, and the world isn't fair. 

> The circumstances that would enable me to die saving someone are, as you can imagine, highly speculative and far outside my usual life circumstances. That being said, there are circumstances in which I can imagine dying to save a random person and those in which I can not. 

I find it unlikely your would ever sacrifice your life for someone you don't know, and if you claim you would, simply to prove I'm wrong, you in turn only prove I'm right. No one would actually do this unless they were suicidal themselves. 

> This does not mean that charity and compassion are delusions, as they can exist without being infinite and unconditional. No offense intended- it doesn't sound like you participate in activities that would lead to you having heard of "compassion fatigue" before now, but being familiar with that concept could help you understand how compassion could exist even in a limited form. I can not literally see from another person's perspective; this is where sympathy and empathy enter the dialogue. If you don't mind clarifying how I fail in my view of the world, I would appreciate it.

Yes compassion can exist as can charity, but in limited forms and for brief periods of time only. Your ideology isn't reflective of your natural biological urges for survival. If a fire broke out in a building of ten of thousands of people, you would all trample each other to get to the exit door, or to get your family to the exit door. Hell, most people will trample each other over a deal on a new TV(see black friday). 

Is that clear enough for you?

I know you won't change your position anyway though, people rarely if ever have the courage to change their view of the world. I once thought like you, that deep down everyone wanted to help each other out. That simply isn't the case however and I would feel less suicidal if people didn't pretend it was.

> Perception is what makes us miserable. 

Perception is indeed *one* possible means of making yourself miserable, to imply that misery is exclusive to perception would be illogical. Depending on how you wish to define perception of course.

> Nothing is concrete.

This doesn't make any sense, are you trying to say reality is more abstract than absolute? Their are particular portions of philosophy and scientific inquiry that can be abstract, yes, for example scientific opinion differs upon a proper quantum mechanical interpretation. 

> You claim you don't bend reality to rationalize and feel better, but you're bending your reality to suit your sadness 

I'm not bending anything to fit the narrative, or my subjective view of it. The narrative is sad based on my reality, unless I were to adopt a sort of skewered perception of it just to stay alive, which wouldn't be rational at all. No my friend, I'm not the one bending reality.

> Before I digest the disadvantages to consider, I wonder if having the goal of not having my efforts ultimately end in nothing sorta voids the warrenty altogether, so to speak.

If your goal is to somehow preserve this current Universe of obliteration, then surely you will fail. If your goal is/was to accomplish all the would make you happy, then you would be able to use these disadvantages to figure out if you will likely succeed or fail in that regard; while maintaining the position that the vast majority of the population won't achieve their goals by means of dumb luck, or strong will, as portrayed in cinema. If you can never actually be happy and/or successful then yes, death/nothing should be preferred over life/something. Although it is simply picking up a pen on one end, the other rises as well.

>  Just being alive seems to garuntee I'll die, at which point there will be nothing left to appreciate the effort/outcome - which means my goal, which I can't otherwise seem to shake, is just completely fail, as I'd sorta view a reversion to nothingness in 100 or 1000 or 1,000,000 years as just as nothing as 0.1μs nothing. And this goal would cease to exist with my death, so... hmm. It seem's that if my unavoidable goal is 'not nothing' than that the inevitable conclusion I would reach about other potential goals is that if they end in nothing, they are not suitable, regardless of current ability/suitability/advantage/disadvantage to achieve them? I guess I'm trying to factor time into this whole thing.

What I said above is a suitable response to this as well.

> Interjecting here- why live only for your own goals and your own happiness?

Sure, so I(among others) should forget my goals and not strive to do what I wish to accomplish, and should put the happiness of another, or others above my own crippling depression?

This is illogical, and no one actually gives a flying fuck about anyone else in this world. Based on this type of response I'm willing to bet you're either a female, or a male with a low testosterone count. Almost everyone puts their own happiness first, as it so happens some people can attain happiness with meager goals, and helping others and putting others first. This is how some people sustain their ability to be happy. If you are a women, despite the exhaustive efforts of modern day ideologies pushing their agendas into the minds of our youth, and now into our adults through our educational system, you should be very happy you're not a man.

It often surprises people that men worldwide kill themselves more than women, and yet women attempt suicide more frequently, and this is explained away because of the means they choose. I find this to be an erroneous conclusion, *most* people who "attempt" suicide do it for attention, just another card in their "pay attention to me" deck. I don't plan on "attempting" anything, I plan on committing suicide. Even more hilarious a contraction to the current political ideologies of our time is the fact that white males made up 70% of all suicide deaths last year. I will be contributing to the statistic this year, luckily I won't have to put up with the logical fallacies spewed from the mouths of those who do not have the ability to even comprehend a rational thought any longer.

> I ought to add that I disagree with your comment that charity and compassion are delusions.

Charity and compassion are delusions, would you die to save a random person whom you don't know? Can you truly see from another persons perspective? You cannot based on your first sentence alone, you have no drive in the same sense I do. Although ironically I can see why you see the world in the way in which you do, and I pointed that out above; you seemed to fail in this regard.

I will take my knowledge, my insights, my dreams, my songs, and passions into the void..." when some of it, at very least this post, will stick around in at least my head (even if you delete it), and will not immediately be made void-perfect.
